title: FIIs Raised Stakes in These Indian Stocks for Three Straight Quarters — Some Surged 130%
excerpt: Foreign institutional investors have quietly built positions in a select group of Indian stocks over three consecutive quarters, with GE Vernova T&D India, National Aluminium, and Hitachi Energy India delivering multibagger returns.
body:
• FIIs increased stakes in 9 Indian stocks for three consecutive quarters through March 2026, with share prices rallying up to 115%
  • GE Vernova T&D India led the pack with a 115% gain as FII holdings rose from 14.49% to 20.39%; National Aluminium and Hitachi Energy India both doubled
  • Among smallcaps, Sterlite Technologies surged 451% over six months while FII ownership jumped from 10.93% to 18.22% across two quarters
  • Market experts warn that after rapid rerating, valuations leave limited room for earnings disappointments in mid- and small-cap segments

Foreign institutional investors have been running a quiet accumulation strategy across Indian equities, steadily raising stakes in a select group of stocks for three straight quarters. The results have been striking: three of these stocks turned multibagger, and the broader group delivered returns ranging from 42% to 115% over the past year, according to ACE Equity data.

The Three-Quarter Accumulation

GE Vernova T&D India emerged as the top performer, with its stock price surging 115% from ₹2,299 to ₹4,937 over the past year. FII holdings climbed from 14.49% in June 2025 to 20.39% by March 2026 — a nearly 6-percentage-point increase that signals deep conviction in India's power transmission sector.

National Aluminium Company delivered a 102% gain, rising from ₹187 to ₹377, as FII ownership expanded from 15.06% to 22.27%. Hitachi Energy India matched that return, advancing from ₹17,039 to ₹34,337 while foreign holdings grew from 7.19% to 11.68%. Both stocks crossed the multibagger threshold.

Apar Industries rallied 91% to ₹15,238 with FII stake growing from 9.06% to 9.38%. Cummins India gained 69% as foreign holdings rose from 17.50% to 20.77%. Bank of Maharashtra — a public sector bank — jumped 61% with FII ownership tripling from 1.89% to 5.55%, one of the sharpest percentage-point increases in the group.

"After their sharp three-month rebound, valuations in this space leave a narrow margin of safety and little room to absorb earnings disappointments."

— Rajesh Palviya, Head of Research, Axis Direct

Smallcap Multibaggers Attract Foreign Money

The trend extends deeper into smaller companies. A separate analysis from Economic Times found 11 smallcap stocks that at least doubled in six months while FII ownership rose across both the March and June 2026 quarters.

Sterlite Technologies led with a 451% surge to ₹518 from ₹94, as FII ownership jumped from 10.93% in December 2025 to 18.22% in June 2026. MTAR Technologies stood out for the scale of accumulation — its shares climbed 126% while foreign ownership more than doubled to 24.79% from 12.24%, a 12.55-percentage-point increase that was the largest among the 11 multibaggers.

Other notable names included Dee Development (up 234%), Indo Tech Transformers (up 139%), KSH International (up 138%), and Aeroflex Industries (up 134%). Rashi Peripherals doubled to ₹736 as its FII holding surged from 0.66% to 3.27%.

Power, Manufacturing, and Defense Lead Themes

The sectoral pattern is clear. FII accumulation has concentrated in power transmission and distribution, renewable energy equipment, specialty chemicals, defence manufacturing, and electronics — sectors tied to India's infrastructure buildout and manufacturing ambitions under production-linked incentive schemes.

Navin Fluorine International gained 61% with FII holdings rising from 21.55% to 23.78%. Polycab India — a key play on India's electrical infrastructure — appreciated 58% as foreign stake grew from 11.45% to 18.21%. Hindalco Industries advanced 57% with FII ownership ticking up from 27.60% to 29.96%.

"Some stocks have become expensive, and we're cognizant of that; we'll take profit-booking action wherever the risk-reward turns unattractive."

— Mayur Patel, President and Fund Manager, 360 ONE Asset

Caution Ahead

The simultaneous rise in share prices and foreign ownership signals conviction, not indiscriminate buying. But the pace of rerating has compressed future return potential. Rajesh Palviya of Axis Direct noted that 93% of sectors have outperformed frontline indices in FY27 so far, even though only 46% of NSE 500 stocks trade above their 200-day moving averages — a divergence suggesting strong sectoral performance but an uneven underlying market.

He expects Nifty earnings to return to double-digit growth with an estimated 11.2% year-on-year expansion in Q1 FY27, but adds that a sustained directional rally requires greater macroeconomic stability. For now, the market remains range-bound and driven by stock-specific opportunities rather than broad momentum. FIIs have shown they are willing to look beyond headline indices, but after gains of up to 451%, the next phase will depend on whether earnings can justify the rerating.
nri_angle: NRI investors tracking Indian markets can use FII accumulation patterns as a signal for identifying stocks with institutional conviction and momentum.
